name: Orokk Omosh
summary: In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh keeps his family's smithing craft alive. The aging orc has no children to inherit it, so he seeks worthy Horde apprentices to learn the Omosh armorcraft secrets.

sections.title: A Lineage at Its End
sections.body: In the Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh is the last smith of the Omosh line. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. Capable Horde blacksmiths can undertake his demanding trials of metalwork. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft.

sections.title: The Spirit of the Forge
sections.body: Among fellow artisans, Orokk is known for his boisterous delight in true mastery. Those who complete his craftsmanship trials often see him perform the Omosh Dance of Joy, a jubilant celebration of traditional smithing that echoes through Orgrimmar's halls.

faq.answer: Orokk Omosh is an aging orc blacksmith in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He is the last smith of the Omosh lineage and seeks worthy Horde apprentices to preserve his family's craft.

faq.q: Where can Orokk Omosh be found?
faq.answer: You can find Orokk Omosh beside the smithing forges and anvils in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, in the city's northeastern section.

faq.q: Why is Orokk Omosh teaching outsiders his family secrets?
faq.answer: Orokk has no children to inherit his family's craft. He teaches skilled Horde blacksmiths who prove capable in his trials so the Omosh techniques do not die with him.

faq.q: What is the 'Omosh Dance of Joy'?
faq.answer: The Omosh Dance of Joy is a jubilant jig Orokk performs when an artisan proves their worth and masters his line's smithing techniques. It is his spirited tribute to the craft.

angles.text: As a Horde blacksmith, you can learn from Orokk Omosh and help preserve his family's ancestral craft.
As a member of the Horde, you can help keep traditional orcish plate and mail techniques available to the warriors defending the fledgling Horde.
